note: Per-DISCIPLINE tuning models. Each captures the variables that actually determine performance, a near-formula baseline (the 'template'), sub-variants, and HOW MUCH bespoke tuning matters (convergence). This is the layer between tuning-variables.json (the UI structure) and per-car tunes: for high-convergence disciplines (drag) you APPLY THE TEMPLATE instead of hunting per-car codes; for low-convergence ones (circuit) bespoke tunes + driver line dominate.

convergence_scale.high: Cars are nearly FLAT within a class (fractions of a second). The tune is a near-solved formula; car choice barely matters. -> APPLY THE TEMPLATE; don't code-hunt.
convergence_scale.medium: Cars cluster but setup + car traits (traction, compliance) create real gaps. Template gets you ~80%; refine for the car/route.
convergence_scale.low: Wide spread; bespoke tune + racing line + car choice all matter (e.g. a 27s circuit-board spread). -> download the fastest clean-lap tune; the template is only a starting point.

templates.label: Drag (straight line)
templates.convergence_note: Within a class the field is FLAT — fractions of a second. PI caps power-to-weight and the tune is a formula, so car choice barely matters. NOT flat across classes, and strip length shifts the winner.
templates.tune_sourcing: APPLY THIS TEMPLATE — per-car drag codes barely differ; don't waste time hunting them (that's also where fake TikTok codes live). Just apply the formula to any good-launching car.
key_variables: 1. Gearing matched to the strip — THE lever (tune on-track)
2. Launch traction: drivetrain + weight transfer (AWD hooks best off the line)
3. Power-to-weight — but PI-capped, so cars cluster; pick a PI-efficient chassis
4. Strip length (1/8 vs 1/4 vs 1-mile) — decides launch-vs-top-speed bias

template.gearing: Tune on-track: SHORT final drive for 1/8-mile, LONGER for the 1-mile; hit the rev limiter right at the line. Biggest single lever.
template.differential: High accel lock (AWD ~100 F / 100 R, center ~55-60% rear); low decel lock.
template.tires: Rear ~15-20 psi (launch contact patch), Front ~45-50 psi (cut rolling drag). Drag compound.
template.aero: MINIMUM both ends (toward Speed) — downforce is pure drag in a straight line.
template.springs_ride_damping: Stiff / low / stiff — not a meaningful drag lever.
template.launch: Rev to peak torque, feed throttle to balance bog-vs-spin. AWD lets you be aggressive.

variants.name: 1/8 mile
variants.deltas: Shortest gearing, launch-max; AWD dominates (Dodge Demon, Miata FE).

variants.name: 1/4 mile
variants.deltas: Balanced; tuned Jesko / Sian trade wins with the FE cars.

variants.name: 1-mile airstrip
variants.deltas: Longest gearing, top-speed king (Hennessey Venom F5), aero-min; RWD fine.

templates.car_selection: Pick by launch + PI-efficiency, not raw name. Best: Miata FE (aftermarket spawn, medium) and GT-R Black FE (Wheelspin, hard). AWD for short strips; light/RWD + aero-min for the mile.

templates.label: Road / Circuit
templates.convergence_note: Wide spread — grip, braking, rotation, aero balance, gearing and the DRIVER's line all interact. On a soft board a clean lap in a competent car beats the field; on a solved board the bespoke tune + line decide it.
templates.tune_sourcing: DOWNLOAD the fastest clean-lap tune from the Rivals leaderboard, or in-game Tune Browser > Surface: ROAD. Bespoke tunes genuinely matter here — the template is only a starting point.
key_variables: 1. Racing line / clean laps (driver — often the biggest gap of all)
2. Grip: tire compound + pressure
3. Braking stability + corner entry
4. Corner-exit traction (diff + deployable power)
5. Rotation (ARB balance, mechanical balance ~0.55-0.65)
6. Aero balance (~0.40-0.50) and gearing matched to the track

template.tires: ~28 F / 27 R psi cold (target 31-33 hot). Road Race compound or Slicks.
template.anti_roll_bars: Stiffer REAR than front to rotate (fights the usual understeer); tune toward Mech. Balance ~0.60.
template.springs_ride_height: Moderate-stiff for tarmac; ride height low (to the slider min for the car).
template.differential: Accel ~40-60% (deployable exit), center ~70% rear on AWD; NOT locked.
template.gearing: Tune to the track — short final drive for technical, longer for high-speed.

variants.name: Technical / street circuit
variants.deltas: More downforce, SHORT gearing, grip-max. UNDER-PI can win (lighter/more controllable) — see Electric Town.

variants.name: High-speed circuit
variants.deltas: Less aero, LONGER gearing, top-end matters more.

templates.car_selection: Car choice + bespoke tune both matter. But read the board first: a soft/uncontested board makes the car nearly irrelevant vs a clean lap.

templates.label: Touge / Street
templates.convergence_note: Like Road but tighter and more technical, with walls close. Rewards rotation, braking, and corner-exit over top speed even more than circuit.
templates.tune_sourcing: Leaderboard-download or in-game Surface: Road/Street. Bespoke tunes matter.
key_variables: 1. Line + braking points (driver)
2. Turn-in / rotation (caster, ARB rear bias)
3. Corner-exit traction (diff)
4. Grip, and SHORT gearing for the hairpins

template.anti_roll_bars: Slightly more rear bias for sharper rotation.
template.aero: More downforce; top speed is nearly irrelevant.

variants.name: Downhill
variants.deltas: Braking stability paramount; slightly forward brake bias.

variants.name: Uphill/mixed
variants.deltas: Corner-exit traction and power delivery matter more.

templates.car_selection: Nimble AWD (forgiving) or a light RWD you can rotate. Same as Road picks.

templates.label: Dirt / Rally
templates.convergence_note: Cars cluster but drivetrain (AWD) and suspension compliance create real gaps. Template gets you most of the way; refine for the route roughness.
templates.tune_sourcing: In-game Tune Browser > Surface: Dirt / Rally, or leaderboard-download.
key_variables: 1. AWD traction on a loose surface
2. Suspension COMPLIANCE (soft springs + damping — soak bumps, keep tires planted)
3. Ride height raised (avoid bottoming)
4. Rally tires; diff decel lock for off-throttle stability

template.differential: Higher DECEL lock for stability; moderate accel; rear-ish center (AWD).
template.alignment: Less negative camber than road; toe ~0.
template.gearing: For the route; usually shorter than road.

variants.name: Smooth dirt
variants.deltas: Firmer than rough; a touch lower ride height.

variants.name: Rough rally
variants.deltas: Softest suspension, highest ride height, most compliance.

templates.car_selection: AWD dominates. Compliance and traction beat outright grip. Focus RS / Evo / STI / Golf R class.

templates.label: Cross Country
templates.convergence_note: Roughest surface with jumps. The car's off-road stat and durability matter as much as tune; AWD is near-mandatory.
templates.tune_sourcing: In-game Tune Browser > Surface: Cross Country, or leaderboard-download.
key_variables: 1. AWD + high off-road stat car
2. Max suspension travel / softest damping (land jumps, keep contact)
3. Max ride height (clear obstacles)
4. Off-road tires; durability

template.springs_damping: Softest that doesn't bottom or wallow.
template.differential: Traction-biased with decel stability for landings.

templates.car_selection: High off-road-stat AWD: Can-Am Maverick (B), the trucks, Viper GTS ACR FE / BRZ FE (A). Off-road stat > power here.
